subject: chemistry
title: Cracking
key_idea: Cracking breaks large, less useful hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful ones. It uses high temperature with a catalyst or steam. The products are smaller alkanes and alkenes, which are in high demand as fuels and for making polymers.

blocks.text: Cracking turns large hydrocarbons from the fractions of crude oil into smaller ones.

items.meaning: Breaking down large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful molecules.
A hydrocarbon with a C=C double bond. It is unsaturated.

items: The large molecules are saturated alkanes.
The products include smaller alkanes and alkenes.
The total number of each type of atom stays the same, so the equation must balance.

blocks.label: An example of cracking
where: C₁₀H₂₂ is decane, a large alkane
C₈H₁₈ is octane, a smaller alkane

diagram.alt: A large alkane is heated with a catalyst or steam and becomes a smaller alkane and an alkene.
steps: High temperature with a catalyst or steam

diagram.alt: Practise working out the hydrogen atoms in the alkane made when decane is cracked.
diagram.question: Decane, C₁₀H₂₂, is cracked into one alkene molecule with **{k}** carbon atoms and one alkane molecule. Alkenes have the formula CₙH₂ₙ. How many hydrogen atoms are in the alkane molecule?
working: The alkene has {k} carbon atoms, so it has 2 × {k} hydrogen atoms.

items: Cracking breaks large alkanes into smaller alkanes and alkenes.
Equations for cracking must have the same atoms on both sides.

blocks.text: Cracking needs a high temperature. There are two main methods.

items: **Catalytic cracking:** uses a catalyst at a high temperature.
**Steam cracking:** uses steam at a high temperature.
Cracking uses a high temperature with a catalyst or steam.
The two methods are catalytic cracking and steam cracking.

blocks.text: Crude oil does not contain the fractions in the amounts that people need.

items: There is a high demand for fuels with small molecules, such as petrol.
Crude oil does not supply enough small molecules, and there is a surplus of large molecules.
Small molecules are more flammable, so they are better fuels.
Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes. They are used to make polymers and as starting materials for many other chemicals.

rows: In high demand as fuels, because small molecules are more flammable
Used to produce polymers and as starting materials for other chemicals

items: Cracking makes more of the small molecules that are in high demand.
Smaller alkanes are used as fuels. Alkenes are used to make polymers and other chemicals.

checks.q: Give two conditions used for cracking.

checks.q: Explain why large hydrocarbon molecules in the diesel oil fraction are cracked.
checks.a: There is a greater demand for smaller molecules. Smaller molecules are more useful, for example better fuels, or are used to make alkenes or polymers.

worked_example.question:
The heavy fuel oil fraction can be processed to produce smaller hydrocarbon molecules.

Name the process which produces smaller hydrocarbon molecules from heavy fuel oil.

Give the conditions used in this process.
answer_points: High temperature (a stated temperature in the range 300 to 900 °C is allowed).
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the name, the temperature and the steam or catalyst.

worked_example.question:
Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons.
Crude oil can be separated into useful fractions by the process of fractional distillation in a fractionating column.

Hydrocarbon X was cracked to form one molecule of hexane, C₆H₁₄, and one molecule of alkene Y.
X → C₆H₁₄ + Y
The relative formula mass of Y is 56.
The empirical formula of Y is CH₂.
Deduce the molecular formula of hydrocarbon X.
Show your working.
(relative atomic masses: H = 1.0, C = 12)
answer_points: Formula of X = C₆H₁₄ + C₄H₈ = C₁₀H₂₂.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step. Marks can follow through from an earlier error if the working is shown.

worked_example.question:
After crude oil is separated into fractions, some fractions are then cracked.

Explain why some fractions are cracked.
answer_points: Any three from: high demand for smaller molecules; smaller molecules are used for fuels and alkenes are used for polymers; not enough supply of smaller molecules; a surplus of larger molecules; cracking changes larger molecules into smaller molecules or alkenes.
worked_example.tip: Named examples are allowed, such as bitumen as the larger molecule and LPG or petrol as the smaller.
